Contents of https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/calibration.html:
When performing classification you often want not only to predict the class label, but also obtain a probability of the respective label. This probability gives you some kind of confidence on the prediction. Some models can give you poor estimates of the class probabilities and some even do not support probability prediction (e.g., some instances of [`SGDClassifier`](generated/sklearn.linear_model.SGDClassifier.html#sklearn.linear_model.SGDClassifier "sklearn.linear_model.SGDClassifier")). The calibration module allows you to better calibrate the probabilities of a given model, or to add support for probability prediction.

Well calibrated classifiers are probabilistic classifiers for which the output of the [predict\_proba](../glossary.html#term-predict_proba) method can be directly interpreted as a confidence level. For instance, a well calibrated (binary) classifier should classify the samples such that among the samples to which it gave a [predict\_proba](../glossary.html#term-predict_proba) value close to, say, 0.8, approximately 80% actually belong to the positive class.

Before we show how to re-calibrate a classifier, we first need a way to detect how good a classifier is calibrated.

Note

Strictly proper scoring rules for probabilistic predictions like [`sklearn.metrics.brier_score_loss`](generated/sklearn.metrics.brier_score_loss.html#sklearn.metrics.brier_score_loss "sklearn.metrics.brier_score_loss") and [`sklearn.metrics.log_loss`](generated/sklearn.metrics.log_loss.html#sklearn.metrics.log_loss "sklearn.metrics.log_loss") assess calibration (reliability) and discriminative power (resolution) of a model, as well as the randomness of the data (uncertainty) at the same time. This follows from the well-known Brier score decomposition of Murphy [\[1\]](#id13). As it is not clear which term dominates, the score is of limited use for assessing calibration alone (unless one computes each term of the decomposition). A lower Brier loss, for instance, does not necessarily mean a better calibrated model, it could also mean a worse calibrated model with much more discriminatory power, e.g. using many more features.

## 1.16.1. Calibration curves[#](#calibration-curves "Link to this heading")

Calibration curves, also referred to as _reliability diagrams_ (Wilks 1995 [\[2\]](#id14)), compare how well the probabilistic predictions of a binary classifier are calibrated. It plots the frequency of the positive label (to be more precise, an estimation of the _conditional event probability_ \\(P(Y=1|\\text{predict\_proba})\\)) on the y-axis against the predicted probability [predict\_proba](../glossary.html#term-predict_proba) of a model on the x-axis. The tricky part is to get values for the y-axis. In scikit-learn, this is accomplished by binning the predictions such that the x-axis represents the average predicted probability in each bin. The y-axis is then the _fraction of positives_ given the predictions of that bin, i.e. the proportion of samples whose class is the positive class (in each bin).

The top calibration curve plot is created with [`CalibrationDisplay.from_estimator`](generated/sklearn.calibration.CalibrationDisplay.html#sklearn.calibration.CalibrationDisplay.from_estimator "sklearn.calibration.CalibrationDisplay.from_estimator"), which uses [`calibration_curve`](generated/sklearn.calibration.calibration_curve.html#sklearn.calibration.calibration_curve "sklearn.calibration.calibration_curve") to calculate the per bin average predicted probabilities and fraction of positives. [`CalibrationDisplay.from_estimator`](generated/sklearn.calibration.CalibrationDisplay.html#sklearn.calibration.CalibrationDisplay.from_estimator "sklearn.calibration.CalibrationDisplay.from_estimator") takes as input a fitted classifier, which is used to calculate the predicted probabilities. The classifier thus must have [predict\_proba](../glossary.html#term-predict_proba) method. For the few classifiers that do not have a [predict\_proba](../glossary.html#term-predict_proba) method, it is possible to use [`CalibratedClassifierCV`](generated/sklearn.calibration.CalibratedClassifierCV.html#sklearn.calibration.CalibratedClassifierCV "sklearn.calibration.CalibratedClassifierCV") to calibrate the classifier outputs to probabilities.

The bottom histogram gives some insight into the behavior of each classifier by showing the number of samples in each predicted probability bin.

[![../_images/sphx_glr_plot_compare_calibration_001.png](../_images/sphx_glr_plot_compare_calibration_001.png)](../auto_examples/calibration/plot_compare_calibration.html)

[`LogisticRegression`](generated/sklearn.linear_model.LogisticRegression.html#sklearn.linear_model.LogisticRegression "sklearn.linear_model.LogisticRegression") is more likely to return well calibrated predictions by itself as it has a canonical link function for its loss, i.e. the logit-link for the [Log loss](model_evaluation.html#log-loss). In the unpenalized case, this leads to t

Before running XGBoost, we must set three types of parameters: general parameters, booster parameters and task parameters.

*   **General parameters** relate to which booster we are using to do boosting, commonly tree or linear model
    
*   **Booster parameters** depend on which booster you have chosen
    
*   **Learning task parameters** decide on the learning scenario. For example, regression tasks may use different parameters with ranking tasks.
    

Note

Parameters in R package

## Global Configuration[](#global-configuration "Link to this heading")

The following parameters can be set in the global scope, using [`xgboost.config_context()`](python/python_api.html#xgboost.config_context "xgboost.config_context") (Python) or `xgb.set.config()` (R).

*   `verbosity`: Verbosity of printing messages. Valid values of 0 (silent), 1 (warning), 2 (info), and 3 (debug).
    
*   `use_rmm`: Whether to use RAPIDS Memory Manager (RMM) to allocate cache GPU memory. The primary memory is always allocated on the RMM pool when XGBoost is built (compiled) with the RMM plugin enabled. Valid values are `true` and `false`. See [Using XGBoost with RAPIDS Memory Manager (RMM) plugin](python/rmm-examples/index.html) for details.
    
*   `use_cuda_async_pool` \[default=false\]
    
    Whether to use the device memory pool in the CUDA driver. This option is not available if XGBoost is built with RMM support, as it is the same as using the RMM CudaAsyncMemoryResource pool.
    
    Added in version 3.2.0.
    
    Warning
    
    This is an experimental feature and is subject to change without notice. Windows is not supported yet.
    
*   `nthread`: Set the global number of threads for OpenMP. Use this only when you need to override some OpenMP-related environment variables like `OMP_NUM_THREADS`. Otherwise, the `nthread` parameter from the Booster and the DMatrix should be preferred as the former sets the global variable and might cause conflicts with other libraries.
    

## General Parameters[](#general-parameters "Link to this heading")

*   `booster` \[default= `gbtree`\]
    
    *   Which booster to use. Can be `gbtree`, `gblinear` or `dart`; `gbtree` and `dart` use tree based models while `gblinear` uses linear functions.
        
*   `device` \[default= `cpu`\]
    
    Added in version 2.0.0

Contents of https://dcase.community/challenge2024/task-sound-event-detection-with-heterogeneous-training-dataset-and-potentially-missing-labels:
The goal of this task is to evaluate systems for the detection of sound events using real data, with different types of annotations data and corresponding labels available for training.

**Challenge has ended.** Full results for this task can be found in the [Results](/challenge2024/task-sound-event-detection-with-heterogeneous-training-dataset-and-potentially-missing-labels-results) page.

## Description

This task is the follow up to [task 4 A](https://dcase.community/challenge2023/task-sound-event-detection-with-weak-labels-and-synthetic-soundscapes) and [task 4 B](https://dcase.community/challenge2023/task-sound-event-detection-with-soft-labels) in 2023. We propose to unify the setup of both subtasks. The target of this task is to provide the event class together with the event time boundaries, given that multiple events can be present and may be overlapping in an audio recording. This task aims at exploring how to leverage training data with varying annotation granularity (temporal resolution, soft/hard labels).

## Novelties for 2024 edition

*   Systems will be evaluated on **labels with different granularity** in order to get a broader view of the systems behavior and to assess their robustness for different applications.
*   The target classes in the different datasets are different, and hence sound labels of one dataset **may be present but not annotated** in the other one. The systems will have to cope with potentially missing target labels at training.
*   The SED system will have to perform **without knowing the origin of the audio clips** at evaluation time.

## Scientific questions

This task highlights a number of specific research questions:

*   What is the most efficient way to exploit different sources of data to train a sound event detection system?
*   Is annotation uncertainty useful in learning models for SED?
*   How to exploit training data with partially missing annotations? How can we evaluate SED systems in a robust way?
*   How can we train SED systems that should perform well under various sound event distribution with potentail domain mismatch?

## Audio dataset

This task is based on the **DESED dataset** and the **MAESTRO Real** dataset.

## DESED dataset

DESED dataset has been used since [DCASE 2020 Task 4](https://dcase.community/challenge2020/task-sound-event-detection-and-separation-in-domestic-environments). DESED is composed of 10 sec audio clips recorded in domestic environments (taken from [AudioSet](https://research.google.com/AudioSet/)) or synthesized using [Scaper](https://github.com/justinsalamon/Scaper) to simulate a domestic environment. DESED focuses on 10 classes of sound events that represent a subset of AudioSet (note that not all the classes in DESED correspond to classes in AudioSet; for example, some classes in DESED group several classes from AudioSet).

Publication

Nicolas Turpault, Romain Serizel, Ankit Parag Shah, and Justin Salamon. _Sound event detection in domestic environments with weakly labeled data and soundscape synthesis._ In Workshop on Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events. New York City, United States, October 2019. URL: [https://hal.inria.fr/hal-02160855](https://hal.inria.fr/hal-02160855).

#### Sound event detection in domestic environments with weakly labeled data and soundscape synthesis

##### Abstract

This paper presents Task 4 of the Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events (DCASE) 2019 challenge and provides a first analysis of the challenge results. The task is a followup to Task 4 of DCASE 2018, and involves training systems for large-scale detection of sound events using a combination of weakly labeled data, i.e. training labels without time boundaries, and strongly-labeled synthesized data. The paper introduces Domestic Environment Sound Event Detection (DESED) dataset mixing a part of last year dataset and an additional synthetic, strongly labeled, dataset provided this year that we’ll describe more i

Comparative Study

. 1988 Sep;44(3):837-45.

Affiliations

*   PMID: **3203132**

Comparative Study

## Comparing the areas under two or more correlated receiver operating characteristic curves: a nonparametric approach

E R DeLong et al. Biometrics. 1988 Sep.

## Abstract

Methods of evaluating and comparing the performance of diagnostic tests are of increasing importance as new tests are developed and marketed. When a test is based on an observed variable that lies on a continuous or graded scale, an assessment of the overall value of the test can be made through the use of a receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve. The curve is constructed by varying the cutpoint used to determine which values of the observed variable will be considered abnormal and then plotting the resulting sensitivities against the corresponding false positive rates. When two or more empirical curves are constructed based on tests performed on the same individuals, statistical analysis on differences between curves must take into account the correlated nature of the data. This paper presents a nonparametric approach to the analysis of areas under correlated ROC curves, by using the theory on generalized U-statistics to generate an estimated covariance matrix.

[View PDF](/pdf/1912.10211)

> Abstract:Audio pattern recognition is an important research topic in the machine learning area, and includes several tasks such as audio tagging, acoustic scene classification, music classification, speech emotion classification and sound event detection. Recently, neural networks have been applied to tackle audio pattern recognition problems. However, previous systems are built on specific datasets with limited durations. Recently, in computer vision and natural language processing, systems pretrained on large-scale datasets have generalized well to several tasks. However, there is limited research on pretraining systems on large-scale datasets for audio pattern recognition. In this paper, we propose pretrained audio neural networks (PANNs) trained on the large-scale AudioSet dataset. These PANNs are transferred to other audio related tasks. We investigate the performance and computational complexity of PANNs modeled by a variety of convolutional neural networks. We propose an architecture called Wavegram-Logmel-CNN using both log-mel spectrogram and waveform as input feature. Our best PANN system achieves a state-of-the-art mean average precision (mAP) of 0.439 on AudioSet tagging, outperforming the best previous system of 0.392. We transfer PANNs to six audio pattern recognition tasks, and demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in several of those tasks. We have released the source code and pretrained models of PANNs: [this https URL](https://github.com/qiuqiangkong/audioset_tagging_cnn).

232. up: desktop-setup | $(RUN_DIR) $(LOCK_DIR)

235. 		if [[ -f "$(APP_PID_FILE)" ]]; then \
236. 			pid="$$(cat "$(APP_PID_FILE)")"; \
237. 			if kill -0 "$$pid" 2>/dev/null; then \

239. 				exit 0; \
240. 			fi; \
241. 			rm -f "$(APP_PID_FILE)"; \
242. 		fi; \
243. 		compute_build_sig() { \

245. 				printf "node=%s\n" "$$("$(NODE)" -v)"; \
246. 				cd "$(DESKTOP_DIR_ABS)"; \

248. 				sha256sum package.json astro.config.mjs tsconfig.json bun.lock; \
249. 			} | sha256sum | cut -d" " -f1; \
250. 		}; \
251. 		signature="$$(compute_build_sig)"; \
252. 		if [[ ! -f "$(BUILD_STAMP_FILE)" || ! -d "$(DESKTOP_DIR_ABS)/dist" || "$$(cat "$(BUILD_STAMP_FILE)")" != "$$signature" ]]; then \
253. 			rm -rf "$(DESKTOP_DIR_ABS)/dist" "$(DESKTOP_DIR_ABS)/release"; \
254. 			cd "$(DESKTOP_DIR_ABS)"; \
255. 			"$(NODE)" ./node_modules/astro/astro.js build >"$(APP_LOG_FILE)" 2>&1; \
256. 			printf "%s\n" "$$signature" > "$(BUILD_STAMP_FILE)"; \
257. 		else \
258. 			: >"$(APP_LOG_FILE)"; \
259. 		fi; \
260. 		setsid bash -lc '"'"'cd "$(DESKTOP_DIR_ABS)"; exec "$(NODE)" ./node_modules/astro/astro.js preview --host "$(APP_HOST)" --port "$(APP_PORT)"'"'"' >>"$(APP_LOG_FILE)" 2>&1 < /dev/null & \
261. 		pid="$$!"; \
262. 		echo "$$pid" >"$(APP_PID_FILE)"; \
263. 		echo "Started $(APP_NAME) (pid $$pid), waiting for $(APP_URL)"; \
264. 		for _ in $$(seq 1 60); do \
265. 			if ! kill -0 "$$pid" 2>/dev/null; then \
266. 				echo "$(APP_NAME) exited during startup"; \
267. 				tail -n 50 "$(APP_LOG_FILE)" || true; \
268. 				rm -f "$(APP_PID_FILE)"; \
269. 				exit 1; \
270. 			fi; \
271. 			if "$(CURL)" -fsS "$(APP_URL)" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
272. 				echo "$(APP_NAME) is ready at $(APP_URL)"; \
273. 				exit 0; \
274. 			fi; \
275. 			sleep 1; \
276. 		done; \
277. 		echo "Timed out waiting for $(APP_NAME) at $(APP_URL)"; \
278. 		tail -n 50 "$(APP_LOG_FILE)" || true; \
279. 		exit 1'

5. ## Scope

7. This audit covers the local Phase 1 inventory only:

9. - reviewed session roots available locally

18. ## Executive Answer

20. The local repo contains enough reviewed evidence to proceed to Phase 2 schema design now.

36. - event boundaries or delayed-entry timing inside a reviewed window

283. 
284. `false_negative_neighborhoods.jsonl` exists for:
285. 
286. - `evaluation_insep_15min_validated`
287. - `evaluation_insep_quick_9015_20260409_ui`
288. 
289. and gives local frontend score traces around reviewed false negatives.
290. 
291. ### What is not directly labeled
292. 
293. The following target classes are not directly reviewed today:
294. 
295. 1. `springboard_dive`
296.    - current reviewed positives are generic `dive`
297.    - turning them into `springboard_dive` requires session-type inference or future relabeling
298. 
299. 2. `platform_dive`
300.    - current reviewed positives are generic `dive`
301.    - turning them into `platform_dive` requires session-type inference or future relabeling
302. 
303. 3. `springboard_rebound_only`
304.    - `non_dive / board_rebound` is the closest direct evidence
305.    - but this is still candidate-level, not reviewed event-window labeling
306. 
307. 4. `noise_or_other`
308.    - partial direct evidence exists through `voice_whistle`, `handling_noise`, `non_dive_splash`, and some unlabeled `non_dive`
309.    - the unified event-window class would still require mapping/inference
310. 
311. Also missing:
312. 
313. - explicit event anchor labels
314. - explicit entry timestamps
315. - explicit board-contact timestamps
316. - explicit event start/end boundaries
317. - reviewed cluster-level annotations saying which peak belongs to the same dive event
318. 
319. ## Are Current Labels Sufficient For Event-Window Training Now
320. 
321. ### Short answer
322. 
323. Not for a clean direct four-class training set.
324. 
325. Partially yes for a weakly supervised prototype.
326. 
327. ### What is sufficient now
328. 
329. Current labels are already sufficient to support:
330. 
331. - event-window schema design
332. - anchor-strategy design
333. - a weakly supervised prototype built from reviewed detections and reviewed false negatives
334. - a first offline binary or coarse multi-class feasibility pass, if the mapping rules are explicitly declared as inferred
335. 
336. Examples of immediately available weak supervision:
337. 
338. - reviewed `dive` candidates in springboard-only session -> likely `springboard_dive` by session-type inference
339. - reviewed `dive` candidates in likely platform INSEP session -> likely `platform_dive` by session-type inference
340. - reviewed `non_dive / board_rebound` -> likely `springboard_rebound_only` candidates, but still not guaranteed event-level purity
341. - reviewed `non_dive / voice_whistle` and `handling_noise` -> likely `noise_or_other`
342. - reviewed false negatives -> positive dive event windows, but still not directly typed as springboard/platform unless session type is known
343. 
344. ### What is not sufficient now
345. 
346. Current labels are not sufficient for a clean claim that the repo already has direct reviewed labels for:
347. 
348. - all four target event classes
349. - event-level archetype boundaries
350. - archetype labels independent of session-level inference
351. 
352. So any Phase 3 dataset built immediately would need explicit label provenance such as:
353. 
354. - `direct_review`
355. - `session_type_inferred`
356. - `subtype_mapped`
357. - `uncertain`
358. 
359. ## Additional Labeling Required
360. 
361. ### Minimum additional labeling to make the four-class task defensible
362. 
363. 1. Confirm session type for ambiguous reviewed sessions.
364.    - `IMG_9015` should be explicitly marked platform or not
365.    - `Champigny` should be explicitly marked springboard or not
366.    - right now both are evidence-backed inferences, not direct metadata facts
367. 
368. 2. Add event-archetype labels for reviewed dive windows.
369.    - `springboard_dive`
370.    - `platform_dive`
371. 
372. 3. Review a subset of `board_rebound` windows at the event level.
373.    - confirm they are truly `springboard_rebound_only`
374.    - confirm there is no valid delayed entry inside the intended event window
375. 
376. 4. Normalize the negative event taxonomy.
377.    - map `voice_whistle`, `handling_noise`, `non_dive_splash`, and null-subtype `non_dive` into a controlled event-level negative taxonomy
378.    - decide whether the first prototype uses one bucket (`noise_or_other`) or preserves subtypes for analysis only
379. 
380. ### Useful but optional extra labeling
381. 
382. 1. Add approximate event anchor or entry timestamps for a subset of dives.
383.    - this would make anchor-strategy evaluation much more rigorous
384. 
385. 2. Add event-window certainty grades.
386.    - direct
387.    - inferred
388.    - ambiguous
389. 
390. 3. Review a small sample of multi-peak springboard clusters explicitly at the event level.
391.    - this would help test whether a proposal-centered window really covers the intended event
392. 
393. ## Practical Recommendation After Phase 1
394. 
395. Proceed directly to Phase 2.
396. 
397. Reason:
398. 
399. - the repo has enough reviewed evidence to define the event-window task carefully
400. - the repo does not yet have enough direct four-class event labels to skip schema work and jump straight to dataset building
401. 
402. So the next step should be:
403. 
404. - define the label taxonomy
405. - define what counts as direct vs inferred labels
406. - define the starting anchor strategy and window length
407. 
408. What should not happen next:
409. 
410. - building a training manifest that silently treats session-type inference as direct truth
411. - claiming current review artifacts already provide a clean four-class event dataset
412.

`outputs/metaexp_es6_embeddings_catalog.json`\n+  - `outputs/metaexp_es6_embedding_head_results.json/.md`\n+  - `outputs/metaexp_es6_residual_cluster_deltas.md`\n+- **Metrics:** AUC/macro F1/guardrails + residual-cluster error deltas.\n+- **Decision rule:**  \n+  - **PASS:** clear robust gain over ES4/ES5 best on both ranking and practical guardrails.  \n+  - **KILL:** no gain after controlled comparison.\n+- **Unlock if pass:** promote embedding path to integration candidate.\n+- **Fallback if fail:** proceed to ES8 governance decision.\n+\n+## ES7 — Calibration + constrained operating-policy search\n+\n+- **Question:** Given best model from ES4/ES5/ES6, is there a defensible operating point satisfying project constraints?\n+- **Hypothesis:** with stronger ranking model, constrained threshold/calibration can satisfy recall/FP guardrails.\n+- **Required inputs:** best model scores on calibration split + frozen holdout predictions.\n+- **Data split rules:** calibration performed off holdout (CV/calibration split); holdout for final evaluation only.\n+- **Allowed changes:** post-hoc calibration and constrained threshold search.\n+- **Forbidden:** re-optimizing feature/model on holdout outcomes.\n+- **Expected artifacts:** `outputs/metaexp_es7_policy_frontier.json/.md`.\n+- **Metrics:** feasibility map over thresholds, Brier/reliability, guardrail satisfaction.\n+- **Decision rule:**  \n+  - **PASS:** at least one operating point satisfies all guardrails with stable behavior.  \n+  - **NEAR_PASS:** close frontier but no feasible point.  \n+  - **KILL:** policy path cannot rescue even improved rankers.\n+- **Unlock if pass:** scientifically defensible Phase 5 r7 integration.\n+- **Fallback if fail:** ES8 governance decision for near-pass closure.\n+\n+## ES8 — Evaluation governance and uncertainty quantification\n+\n+- **Question:** Are near-threshold decisions statistically defensible on current holdout size?\n+- **Hypothesis:** CI-aware governance will reduce false “pass/fail by noise” outcomes.\n+- **Required inputs:** all candidate-model holdout scores and predictions.\n+- **Data split rules:** no training; post-hoc analysis only.\n+- **Allowed changes:** reporting/protocol criteria updates.\n+- **Forbidden:** retroactive metric cherry-picking.\n+- **Expected artifacts:**\n+  - `outputs/metaexp_es8_auc_uncertainty.json/.md`\n+  - `outputs/metaexp_es8_guardband_governance_proposal.md`\n+- **Metrics:** DeLong/Bootstrap AUC intervals, sensitivity to row perturbations.\n+- **Decision rule:**  \n+  - **PASS:** governance rubric accepted and reproducible.  \n+  - **KILL:** if uncertainty too high to support promotion claims.\n+- **Unlock if pass:** stable promotion/near-pass policy for next cycles.\n+- **Fallback if fail:** explicit “insufficient evidence” status + data expansion requirement.\n+\n+## ES9 — Optional semi-supervised / augmentation pilot\n+\n+- **Question:** Can unlabeled proposal pools improve robustness after supervised paths plateau?\n+- **Hypothesis:** modest SSL/augmentation can reduce mixed-cluster variance.\n+- **Required inputs:** labeled frozen set + unlabeled proposal windows with provenance.\n+- **Data split rules:** strict leakage prevention by session and row lineage.\n+- **Allowed changes:** SSL/augmentation modules only in pilot.\n+- **Forbidden:** using unlabeled data that leaks holdout semantics.\n+- **Expected artifacts:** `outputs/metaexp_es9_ssl_pilot.json/.md`.\n+- **Metrics:** delta vs ES4/ES5/ES6 best, variance under resampling.\n+- **Decision rule:**  \n+  - **PASS:** meaningful gain with controlled leakage risk.  \n+  - **KILL:** complexity high, gain low.\n+- **Unlock if pass:** larger SSL program.\n+- **Fallback if fail:** stop SSL line for current cycle.\n+\n+## ES10 — Detector-side alternative interpretation (no behavior change)\n+\n+- **Question:** Can richer interpretation of frozen detector outputs improve downstream decisions without detector edits?\n+- **Hypothesis:** additional proposal diagnostics/provenance features may help policy attribution, not detector changes.\n+- **Required inputs:** candidate diagnostics, proposal metadata, event windows.\n+- **Data split rules:** unchanged from frozen policy.\n+- **Allowed changes:** derived metadata features from existing artifacts only.\n+- **Forbidden:** changing proposal-generation logic, suppression, tie-breaks.\n+- **Expected artifacts:** `outputs/metaexp_es10_detector_interpretation.json/.md`.\n+- **Metrics:** attribution clarity and incremental predictive utility.\n+- **Decision rule:**  \n+  - **PASS:** improved explanatory/decision power with zero detector edits.  \n+  - **KILL:** no measurable utility.\n+- **Unlock if pass:** add interpretation channels to ES4+ datasets.\n+- **Fallback if fail:** drop detector-interpretation line this cycle.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## Part D — Priority ordering (execution roadmap)\n+\n+## Recommended execution order\n+\n+1. **ES4 — Stronger tabular model-family benchmark (top priority).**  \n+2. **ES5 — Ranking-aware objective benchmark.**  \n+3. embeddings** (if ES4/ES5 still near-pass).  \n+6. **ES1/ES10 diagnostics** (lightweight, can run early to sharpen attribution).  \n+7. **ES2/ES3 representation sanity checks** (deferred; current evidence says lower marginal value).  \n+8. **ES9 SSL/augmentation** (high-cost, only after supervised lines plateau).\n+\n+## Why this order\n+\n+1. **Causal clarity:** ES4 most directly tests current leading bottleneck (model-family boundary capacity) while preserving all frozen constraints.\n+2. **Cost/value:** ES4/ES5 are lower engineering cost than embeddings/SSL and produce immediate go/no-go evidence.\n+3. **Decision leverage:** ES7+ES8 are required to convert model gains into defensible promotion decisions.\n+4. **Avoid repeated low-yield loops:** ES2/ES3 are intentionally deprioritized to prevent another feature micro-iteration cycle.\n+\n+## Deferred/high-risk sets\n+\n+- **Deferred:** ES9 until supervised paths are exhausted.\n+- **High-risk/low-value right now:** broad handcrafted feature sweeps and detector patching.\n+- **Prerequisite-gated:** ES6 should be run after ES4/ES5 baseline is established for fair incremental attribution.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## Part E — External research and community patterns (design-relevant)\n+\n+External guidance is used here only to sharpen experiment design, not to override repo evidence.\n+\n+1. **GBDT for tabular interactions** (LightGBM/XGBoost docs/papers): supports ES4 as lowest-friction model-family upgrade for structured features.\n+2. **Ranking-aware objectives** (XGBoost LTR docs): aligns directly with features plateau.\n+4. **Calibration reliability practices** (scikit-learn calibration docs): motivates ES7 to separate ranking quality from probability usability.\n+5. **Uncertainty for ROC comparisons** (DeLong et al., 1988): motivates ES8 so near-threshold decisions are statistically defensible.\n+6. **DCASE heterogeneous-label practice** (DCASE challenge framing): supports disciplined handling of mixed annotation quality, leakage, and governance in ES8/ES9.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## Decision framework (promotion/stop rules)\n+\n+## Global next-cycle success criteria\n+\n+A candidate path is cycle-successful only if all are met:\n+\n+1. Produces at least one guardrail-feasible operating policy (or governance-approved near-pass policy with uncertainty bounds).\n+4. Is reproducible with explicit artifacts and row-level provenance.\n+\n+## Promotion classes\n+\n+- **Promote to Phase 5 r7 integration candidate:** ES4/ES5/ES6 + ES7 pass.\n+- **Near-pass documentation:** technical gains but no feasible operating point; route to ES8 governance decision.\n+- **Kill path:** fails defined success signal or cannot provide stable evidence.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## Risks and anti-patterns to avoid\n+\n+1. Reintroducing ad hoc one-feature tweaks as “progress.”\n+2. Tuning on frozen scored holdout.\n+3. Quietly changing detector behavior while claiming classifier-only work.\n+4. Treating tiny point-metric differences as decisive without uncertainty.\n+5. Mixing track-level and global acceptance logic without explicit governance rule.\n+6. Reopening solved springboard line without new contradicting evidence.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## Part F — Concrete next-cycle recommendation\n+\n+## Single best next-cycle experiment family\n+\n+**Run ES4 (stronger tabular model-family benchmark) first, on frozen r4 representation and frozen data policy.**\n+\n+Why: it is the shortest path to testing the strongest unresolved hypothesis (current boundary/model-family bottleneck) with high causal clarity and low implementation risk.\n+\n+## Best order after that\n+\n+1. ES4 -> 2. ES5 -> 3. ES7 -> 4. ES8 -> 5. ES6 (if needed) -> 6. ES9 only if still unresolved.\n+\n+## Explicitly stop doing\n+\n+- One-off micro-tweak loops (single scalar features, threshold-only retries) without family-level benchmark framing.\n+- Uncertainty-blind pass/fail calls on near-threshold deltas.\n+\n+## Avoid confusing as progress\n+\n+- AUC-only gains that cannot produce feasible operating behavior.\n+- Better threshold snapshots derived by holdout tuning.\n+\n+## Evidence required to declare next cycle successful\n+\n+1. "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/mcauchy/divesensei-app/benchmarks/platform_noise_es4_model_benchmark.py\n@@\n class NumpyLogisticBinary(BaseEstimator, ClassifierMixin):\n+    _estimator_type = \"classifier\"\n+\n     def __init__(self, epochs: int = 1000, lr: float = 0.1, l2: float = 0.01):\n         self.epochs = epochs\n         self.lr = lr\n         self.l2 = l2\n         self.weights_: np.ndarray | None = None\n@@\n     def fit(self, x: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray) -> \"NumpyLogisticBinary\":\n         x = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)\n         y = np.asarray(y, dtype=np.float64)\n         n_samples, n_features = x.shape\n         self.weights_ = np.zeros(n_features, dtype=np.float64)\n         self.bias_ = 0.0\n+        self.classes_ = np.asarray([0, 1], dtype=np.int64)\n+        self.n_features_in_ = n_features\n         for _ in range(self.epochs):\n             logits = x @ self.weights_ + self.bias_\n             probs = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-np.clip(logits, -40.0, 40.0)))\n             error = probs - y\n             grad_w = (x.T @ error) / n_samples + self.l2 * self.weights_\n@@\n     def predict(self, x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n         probs = self.predict_proba(x)[:, 1]\n         return (probs >= 0.5).astype(np.int64)\n+\n+    def _more_tags(self) -> dict[str, Any]:\n+        return {\"binary_only\": True}\n*** End Patch\n"

1. # Handoff — 2026-04-14 Review UI Runtime and Cue Updates
2. 
3. This handoff captures the work completed today on the desktop review flow so you can continue immediately on another machine.
4. 
5. ## Branch / scope
6. 
7. - Branch: `phase4-review-support`
8. - Scope kept fixed:
9.   - detector behavior unchanged
10.   - taxonomy unchanged
11.   - existing reviewed labels unchanged
12.   - no training/model-family expansion in this pass
13. 
14. ## Completed today
15. 
16. 1. UI runtime verification for prepared external session
17. - Verified desktop app runs locally at `http://localhost:5173/`.
18. - Confirmed `evaluation_insep_plateform_mixed_sound` is discoverable in catalog and openable in review.
19. - Confirmed review endpoints load for that session.
20. 
21. 2. Review sidebar regression fix
22. - Root issue: queue sidebar became empty when global refinement queue artifact was absent.
23. - Fix: restored the always-available standard review queue table/filter while preserving refinement queue block when present.
24. 
25. 3. Main controls navigation improvement
26. - Added explicit `Previous` / `Next` buttons in review controls.
27. - Wired to existing wrap-safe queue navigation logic (`selectAdjacentDetection`) to handle first/last item seamlessly.
28. 
29. 4. Decision-save flow stabilization
30. - Root issue: runtime null dereference in event-support sync could interrupt post-save UI updates.
31. - Fix: null-safe access in `syncEventSupportUi` so decision saves continue through live UI update and queue advancement.
32. 
33. 5. Visual splash-cue prototype for no-audio review
34. - Added subtle visual cue tied to loop playback at splash moment:
35.   - compact `Splash cue` indicator in controls
36.   - brief flash on active queue row / refinement row / detail bar
37. - Added optional `Pause at splash` toggle for brief auto-pause+resume at cue time.
38. 
39. 6. False-negative cue anchoring
40. - For manual false negatives (`fn-*`), splash cue now uses the exact reviewer-marked FN timestamp as anchor.
41. - For regular detections, cue anchor prefers support `event_anchor_timestamp_seconds`, fallback to detection timestamp.
42. 
43. ## Files changed for this handoff
44. 
45. - `apps/desktop/src/components/DesignWorkspace.astro`
46. - `apps/desktop/src/styles/global.css`
47. 
48. ## Validation performed

59. 4. In review controls, optional:

61.

122. 
123. Global rule for all sets unless explicitly overridden:
124. 
125. - **Frozen constraints:** detector behavior, taxonomy, reviewed labels, springboard accepted configuration, and baseline slice definitions for comparability.
126. - **Forbidden:** silent detector edits, taxonomy relabeling, retrospective metric reinterpretation, tuning on scored holdout.
127. - **Decision classes:** `PASS`, `NEAR_PASS`, `FAIL/KILL`.

129. ## ES1 — Proposal-family observability and failure-surface map
130. 
131. - **Question:** Are residual failures dominated by missing/poor proposals or by downstream representation/boundary?
132. - **Hypothesis:** Current residual platform/noise near-pass is mostly downstream, not proposal absence.
133. - **Required inputs:** frozen reviewed manifests + `phase5_regime_manifest_lists.json` + phase5 execution/probe outputs.
134. - **Data split rules:** no retraining required; row-level diagnostics over frozen train/holdout.
135. - **Allowed changes:** diagnostics scripts only.
136. - **Forbidden changes:** any proposal generation or threshold behavior changes.
137. - **Expected artifacts:**
138.   - `outputs/metaexp_es1_proposal_failure_surface.json/.md`
139.   - `outputs/metaexp_es1_row_level_tracebacks.jsonl`
140. - **Metrics:** proposal coverage at event-level truth rows, downstream misranking counts conditional on proposal presence.
141. - **Decision rule:**  
142.   - **PASS:** evidence clearly attributes >70% residual errors to downstream boundary/ranking with proposal present.  
143.   - **KILL detector-rework path for now:** if proposal-miss contribution remains minor.
144. - **Interpretation:** establishes whether detector-side work is warranted this cycle.
145. - **Unlock if pass:** prioritize ES4/ES5 over detector rework.
146. - **Fallback if fail:** schedule bounded detector-side diagnostic family before model upgrades.
147.

149. 
150. - **Question:** Is platform/noise still materially limited by temporal framing under frozen anchor policy?
151. - **Hypothesis:** Minor temporal variants will not beat model-family upgrades now.
152. - **Required inputs:** same frozen rows, same labels, same feature extractor backbone.
153. - **Data split rules:** frozen train/holdout; no row movement.
154. - **Allowed changes:** bounded temporal representation variants in offline extraction only.
155. - **Forbidden:** springboard anchor modifications; full taxonomy retraining.
156. - **Expected artifacts:** `outputs/metaexp_es2_temporal_ablation.json/.md`.
157. - **Metrics:** AUC, macro F1, platform recall, noise FP, confusion.
158. - **Decision rule:**  
159.   - **PASS temporal path:** if a temporal-only variant beats current accepted representation and improves guardrail feasibility.  
160.   - **KILL:** if gains are marginal/unstable vs r4 baseline.
161. - **Unlock if pass:** targeted representation refinement before model-family shift.
162. - **Fallback if fail:** proceed to ES4.
163. 
164. ## ES3 — Hand-crafted feature bundle reproducibility and robustness check
165. 
166. - **Question:** Are accepted r4 gains robust under repeated resampling, not just single holdout outcome?
167. - **Hypothesis:** r4 is a real representation gain, but still insufficient alone for guardrail pass.
168. - **Required inputs:** frozen manifests + audio windows + r2/r4 probe feature pipelines.
169. - **Data split rules:** frozen official holdout + repeated stratified resampling on train only.
170. - **Allowed changes:** robustness reporting only.
171. - **Forbidden:** adding new ad hoc feature sweeps.
172. - **Expected artifacts:** `outputs/metaexp_es3_feature_robustness.json/.md`.
173. - **Metrics:** distribution of AUC/macro F1 deltas (r4-r2), variance/CI.
174. - **Decision rule:**  
175.   - **PASS:** r4 > r2 consistently in ranking metrics with acceptable variance.  
176.   - **NEAR_PASS:** directional but unstable.  
177.   - **KILL feature-iteration:** if unstable/noisy and not decision-improving.
178. - **Unlock if pass:** use r4 representation as fixed base for model-family tests.
179. - **Fallback if fail:** freeze at r2 and move immediately to ES4.
180. 
181. ## ES4 — Stronger tabular model-family benchmark (primary)
182. 
183. - **Question:** Can non-linear tabular models convert current representation signal into guardrail-feasible behavior?
184. - **Hypothesis:** Gradient-boosted trees on frozen feature sets outperform logistic on residual mixed cluster.
185. - **Required inputs:** immutable dataset artifact containing row keys, labels, features from accepted representation.
186. - **Data split rules:** frozen official holdout untouched; training uses nested CV for model selection.
187. - **Allowed changes:** model family and hyperparameters only.
188. - **Forbidden:** detector/taxonomy/label/split changes.
189. - **Expected artifacts:**
190.   - `outputs/metaexp_es4_model_family_results.json/.md`
191.   - `outputs/metaexp_es4_feature_interaction_report.md`
192.   - `outputs/metaexp_es4_holdout_predictions.jsonl`
193. - **Metrics:** AUC, macro F1, platform recall, noise recall, FP/FN counts, calibration diagnostics.
194. - **Decision rule:**  
195.   - **PASS:** beats logistic baseline on AUC and produces at least one feasible operating region candidate under guardrails (validated in ES7).  
196.   - **NEAR_PASS:** AUC gain without guardrail-feasible operating point.  
197.   - **KILL:** no robust gain over logistic+r4.
198. - **Unlock if pass:** ES7 constrained policy finalization and Phase 5 r7 candidate integration.
199. - **Fallback if fail:** ES5 (ranking-aware) or ES6 (embeddings).
200. 
201. ## ES5 — Ranking-aware / AUC-first objective benchmark
202. 
203. - **Question:** Does pairwise/ranking optimization reduce ordering overlap better than standard classification loss?
204. - **Hypothesis:** Ranking-aware training improves hard-negative ordering and AUC stability.
205. - **Required inputs:** same immutable feature dataset as ES4; optional grouping by session root.
206. - **Data split rules:** same frozen holdout; strict no-leak query grouping.
207. - **Allowed changes:** objective function (`rank:pairwise` / equivalent), scoring policy.

209. - **Expected artifacts:** `outputs/metaexp_es5_ranking_objective_results.json/.md`.
210. - **Metrics:** AUC, pairwise ordering error on residual cluster, guardrail metrics at candidate thresholds.
211. - **Decision rule:**  
212.   - **PASS:** statistically supported AUC gain and reduced residual overlap vs ES4 best classifier.  
213.   - **KILL:** no stable ordering benefit or severe recall harm.
214. - **Unlock if pass:** ES7 policy calibration on ranking model.
215. - **Fallback if fail:** prioritize ES6 or governance stop decision.

218. 
219. - **Question:** Do pretrained audio embeddings provide more robust separation for mixed noise cluster than hand-crafted features?
220. - **Hypothesis:** frozen embeddings + shallow head improve generalization on small reviewed data.

   - detections with positive decision (`dive` in evaluation mode), and
   - manual false negatives (`fn-*`).

5. Added compact styling for the new checkbox control.

**Dependencies**
No new dependencies were required.

**Command run**
1. `npm --prefix apps/desktop run build`

I tightened the filter logic in `apps/desktop/src/components/DesignWorkspace.astro` so `false_negative` mode explicitly matches FN entries by row type/id (not only decision label), and it now refreshes row references before applying the filter to avoid stale DOM state after updates.

### ✓ Task Complete

Fixed — the **False negatives** queue filter now correctly shows existing/manual FN rows instead of collapsing.

I tightened the filter logic in `apps/desktop/src/components/DesignWorkspace.astro` so `false_negative` mode explicitly matches FN entries by row type/id (not only decision label), and it now refreshes row references before applying the filter to avoid stale DOM state after updates.

1658.       if (!detectionId) return;

1660.       const targetRow = rows.find((row) => row.getAttribute("data-focus-detection") === String(detectionId));

1665.     function timelineFollowDetectionForTime(timeSeconds) {
1666.       const candidates = detections.filter((item) => shouldRenderTimelineMarker(item) && matchesQueueFilter(item));
1667.       if (!candidates.length) return null;
1668.       const containing = candidates.filter((item) => {
1669.         const start = reviewStartFor(item);
1670.         const end = reviewEndFor(item);
1671.         return timeSeconds >= start && timeSeconds < end;
1672.       });
1673.       const pool = containing.length ? containing : candidates;
1674.       return pool.reduce((closest, item) => {
1675.         if (!closest) return item;
1676.         return Math.abs(Number(item.timestamp_seconds ?? 0) - timeSeconds) < Math.abs(Number(closest.timestamp_seconds ?? 0) - timeSeconds)
1677.           ? item
1678.           : closest;

1. import type { APIRoute } from "astro";
2. import {
3.   addEvaluationFalseNegative,
4.   isEvaluationSession,
5.   listEvaluationFalseNegatives,
6.   listEvaluationReviewDecisions,
7.   saveEvaluationFalseNegativeAnnotation,
8.   saveEvaluationReviewDecision,
9. } from "@/lib/evaluation-review-store";
10. import { getManifestPathForAnalysisRun, listReviewDecisions, saveReviewDecision } from "@/lib/session-catalog";
11. import { readManifest } from "@/lib/session-catalog-core";
12. import type { EvaluationReviewSubtype } from "@/types/ui";
13. 
14. const NO_STORE_HEADERS = {
15.   "Cache-Control": "no-store, max-age=0",
16. };
17. 
18. export const GET: APIRoute = async ({ url }) => {
19.   const analysisRunId = url.searchParams.get("analysisRunId");
20.   if (!analysisRunId) {
21.     return Response.json({ error: "analysisRunId is required." }, { status: 400, headers: NO_STORE_HEADERS });
22.   }
23. 
24.   const manifestPath = getManifestPathForAnalysisRun(analysisRunId);
25.   const manifest = manifestPath ? readManifest(manifestPath) : null;
26.   if (isEvaluationSession(manifest)) {
27.     return Response.json({
28.       decisions: manifest ? listEvaluationReviewDecisions(manifest) : [],
29.       falseNegatives: manifest ? listEvaluationFalseNegatives(manifest) : [],
30.       mode: "evaluation",
31.     }, { headers: NO_STORE_HEADERS });
32.   }
33. 
34.   return Response.json({
35.     decisions: listReviewDecisions(analysisRunId),
36.     falseNegatives: [],
37.     mode: "standard",
38.   }, { headers: NO_STORE_HEADERS });
39. };
40. 
41. export const POST: APIRoute = async ({ request }) => {
42.   const body = await request.json().catch(() => null) as
43.     | {
44.         analysisRunId?: string;
45.       detectionId?: string;
46.       label?: "keep" | "reject" | "unsure" | "dive" | "non_dive" | "false_negative";
47.       eventLabel?: "springboard_dive" | "springboard_rebound_only" | "platform_dive" | "noise_or_other" | "uncertain" | null;
48.       subtype?: EvaluationReviewSubtype | null;
49.       notes?: string;
50.       timestampSeconds?: number;
51.     }
52.     | null;
53. 
54.   if (!body?.analysisRunId || !body.label) {
55.     return Response.json({ error: "analysisRunId and label are required." }, { status: 400, headers: NO_STORE_HEADERS });
56.   }
57. 
58.   try {
59.     const manifestPath = getManifestPathForAnalysisRun(body.analysisRunId);
60.     const manifest = manifestPath ? readManifest(manifestPath) : null;
61.     if (isEvaluationSession(manifest)) {
62.       if (!manifest) {
63.         return Response.json({ error: "Evaluation session manifest not found." }, { status: 404, headers: NO_STORE_HEADERS });
64.       }
65.       if (body.label === "false_negative") {
66.         if (body.detectionId) {
67.           const annotation = saveEvaluationFalseNegativeAnnotation(
68.             manifest,
69.             body.analysisRunId,
70.             body.detectionId,
71.             body.eventLabel ?? null,
72.             body.subtype ?? null,
73.             body.notes ?? "",
74.           );
75.           return Response.json({ annotation, mode: "evaluation" }, { headers: NO_STORE_HEADERS });
76.         }
77.         if (typeof body.timestampSeconds !== "number" || Number.isNaN(body.timestampSeconds)) {
78.           return Response.json({ error: "timestampSeconds is required for false_negative." }, { status: 400, headers: NO_STORE_HEADERS });
79.         }
80.         const annotation = addEvaluationFalseNegative(
81.           manifest,
82.           body.analysisRunId,
83.           body.timestampSeconds,
84.           body.eventLabel ?? null,
85.           body.subtype ?? null,
86.           body.notes ?? "",
87.         );
88.         return Response.json({ annotation, mode: "evaluation" }, { headers: NO_STORE_HEADERS });
89.       }
90.       if (!body.detectionId) {
91.         return Response.json({ error: "detectionId is required for evaluation candidate decisions." }, { status: 400, headers: NO_STORE_HEADERS });
92.       }
93.       if (!["dive", "non_dive", "unsure"].includes(body.label)) {
94.         return Response.json({ error: "Invalid evaluation label." }, { status: 400, headers: NO_STORE_HEADERS });
95.       }
96.       const evaluationLabel = body.label as "dive" | "non_dive" | "unsure";
97.       const decision = saveEvaluationReviewDecision(
98.         manifest,
99.         body.analysisRunId,
100.         body.detectionId,
101.         evaluationLabel,
102.         body.eventLabel ?? null,
103.         evaluationLabel === "non_dive" ? body.subtype ?? null : null,
104.         body.notes ?? "",
105.       );
106.       return Response.json({ decision, mode: "evaluation" }, { headers: NO_STORE_HEADERS });
107.     }
108. 
109.     if (!body.detectionId || !["keep", "reject", "unsure"].includes(body.label)) {
110.       return Response.json({ error: "analysisRunId, detectionId, and a standard review label are required." }, { status: 400, headers: NO_STORE_HEADERS });
111.     }
112.     const standardLabel = body.label as "keep" | "reject" | "unsure";
113.     const decision = saveReviewDecision(body.analysisRunId, body.detectionId, standardLabel, body.notes ?? "");
114.     return Response.json({ decision, mode: "standard" }, { headers: NO_STORE_HEADERS });
115.   } catch (error) {
116.     return Response.json({ error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : "Failed to save review decision." }, { status: 400, headers: NO_STORE_HEADERS });
117.   }
118. };
119.

4.   EvaluationFalseNegativeAnnotation,
5.   EvaluationReviewSubtype,
6.   ReviewDecision,
7.   ReviewDecisionLabel,

9. } from "@/types/ui";
10. 
11. interface EvaluationReviewStore {
12.   schemaVersion: string;
13.   decisions: ReviewDecision[];
14.   falseNegatives: EvaluationFalseNegativeAnnotation[];
15. }
16. 
17. const EMPTY_STORE: EvaluationReviewStore = {
18.   schemaVersion: "1.0.0",
19.   decisions: [],
20.   falseNegatives: [],
21. };
22. 
23. function readJsonFile<T>(filePath: string): T | null {
24.   try {
25.     return JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(filePath, "utf-8")) as T;
26.   } catch {
27.     return null;
28.   }
29. }
30. 
31. export function isEvaluationSession(manifest: SessionManifest | null | undefined): boolean {
32.   return (manifest?.session.mode ?? "standard") === "evaluation";
33. }
34. 
35. export function evaluationReviewStorePath(manifest: SessionManifest): string {
36.   const artifactPath = manifest.artifacts?.evaluation_review;
37.   return artifactPath && artifactPath.length > 0
38.     ? artifactPath
39.     : path.join(manifest.session.output_dir, "evaluation_review.json");
40. }
41. 
42. export function loadEvaluationReviewStore(manifest: SessionManifest): EvaluationReviewStore {
43.   const filePath = evaluationReviewStorePath(manifest);
44.   return readJsonFile<EvaluationReviewStore>(filePath) ?? { ...EMPTY_STORE };
45. }
46. 
47. function saveEvaluationReviewStore(manifest: SessionManifest, store: EvaluationReviewStore): void {
48.   const filePath = evaluationReviewStorePath(manifest);
49.   fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(filePath), { recursive: true });
50.   fs.writeFileSync(filePath, JSON.stringify(store, null, 2));
51. }
52. 
53. export function listEvaluationReviewDecisions(manifest: SessionManifest): ReviewDecision[] {
54.   return loadEvaluationReviewStore(manifest).decisions.slice().sort((a, b) => {
55.     if (a.updatedAt === b.updatedAt) return a.detectionId.localeCompare(b.detectionId);
56.     return b.updatedAt.localeCompare(a.updatedAt);
57.   });
58. }
59. 
60. export function saveEvaluationReviewDecision(
61.   manifest: SessionManifest,
62.   analysisRunId: string,
63.   detectionId: string,
64.   label: Extract<ReviewDecisionLabel, "dive" | "non_dive" | "unsure">,
65.   eventLabel: ReviewDecision["eventLabel"] = null,
66.   subtype: EvaluationReviewSubtype | null = null,
67.   notes = "",
68. ): ReviewDecision {
69.   const store = loadEvaluationReviewStore(manifest);
70.   const now = new Date().toISOString();
71.   const existing = store.decisions.find((entry) => entry.analysisRunId === analysisRunId && entry.detectionId === detectionId)
72.     ?? store.decisions.find((entry) => entry.detectionId === detectionId);
73.   const decision: ReviewDecision = {
74.     id: `${analysisRunId}:${detectionId}`,
75.     analysisRunId,
76.     detectionId,
77.     label,
78.     eventLabel,
79.     subtype,
80.     notes,
81.     createdAt: existing?.createdAt ?? now,
82.     updatedAt: now,
83.   };
84.   if (existing) {
85.     Object.assign(existing, decision);
86.   } else {
87.     store.decisions.push(decision);
88.   }
89.   saveEvaluationReviewStore(manifest, store);
90.   return decision;
91. }

93. export function listEvaluationFalseNegatives(manifest: SessionManifest): EvaluationFalseNegativeAnnotation[] {

100. export function addEvaluationFalseNegative(
101.   manifest: SessionManifest,

116.     label: "false_negative",

128. export function saveEvaluationFalseNegativeAnnotation(
129.   manifest: SessionManifest,
130.   analysisRunId: string,
131.   annotationId: string,
132.   eventLabel: EvaluationFalseNegativeAnnotation["eventLabel"] = null,
133.   subtype: EvaluationReviewSubtype | null = null,

137.   const now = new Date().toISOString();

139.   if (!existing) {
140.     throw new Error(`False negative annotation not found: ${annotationId}`);
141.   }
142.   existing.eventLabel = eventLabel;
143.   existing.subtype = subtype;
144.   existing.notes = notes;
145.   existing.updatedAt = now;
146.   saveEvaluationReviewStore(manifest, store);
147.   return existing;
148. }

You were right — I validated the issue.

**What was wrong:** timeline-follow was using a nearest-clip fallback even inside clip gaps, so queue/highlight could jump early while splash cue logic was still tied to the active clip window (`start/end`) in the loop handler.

**Precise fix applied:**
1. `timelineFollowDetectionForTime()` now supports a `allowNearestFallback` mode.
2. During playback-follow, we only switch when the playhead is actually inside a clip window (no gap jumping).
3. Nearest fallback is kept only for manual scrubbing mode.
4. Queue-follow is now gated to true free-timeline contexts (`manualTimelineSeekMode` or FN free-play mode), keeping splash cue timing aligned.

Updated file: `apps/desktop/src/components/DesignWorkspace.astro`.
```

</details>

<sub>⏱️ 2650m 18s</sub>

### ✓ Task Complete

You were right — I validated the issue.

**What was wrong:** timeline-follow was using a nearest-clip fallback even inside clip gaps, so queue/highlight could jump early while splash cue logic was still tied to the active clip window (`start/end`) in the loop handler.

**Precise fix applied:**
1. `timelineFollowDetectionForTime()` now supports a `allowNearestFallback` mode.
2. During playback-follow, we only switch when the playhead is actually inside a clip window (no gap jumping).
3. Nearest fallback is kept only for manual scrubbing mode.
4. Queue-follow is now gated to true free-timeline contexts (`manualTimelineSeekMode` or FN free-play mode), keeping splash cue timing aligned.

Updated file: `apps/desktop/src/components/DesignWorkspace.astro`.

Validated and fixed.

**Troubleshooting result**
1. I verified support anchors are not the cause (`max_anchor_delta_seconds = 0.0` vs detection splash timestamps).
2. Root cause was a stale-window clamp path: splash cue anchor was being resolved with loop-closure `start/end` from a previous clip during timeline-follow transitions, which can shift cues early by up to ~1s in gap boundaries.

**Fix applied**
In `apps/desktop/src/components/DesignWorkspace.astro`:
1. `maybeTriggerSplashCue()` now always derives cue bounds from the **current detection** (`reviewStartFor(current)` / `reviewEndFor(current)`) at trigger time.
2. Removed reliance on stale closure window args for cue anchor/pause checks.

**Validation after fix**
1. Re-ran the anchor diagnostics and confirmed data-side anchor drift is zero.
2. Rebuilt desktop app successfully (`npm --prefix apps/desktop run build`).

This is the precise synchronization fix for the “~1s early splash cue” behavior.

<sub>⏱️ 2659m 46s</sub>

### ✓ Task Complete

Validated and fixed.

**Troubleshooting result**
1. I verified support anchors are not the cause (`max_anchor_delta_seconds = 0.0` vs detection splash timestamps).
2. Root cause was a stale-window clamp path: splash cue anchor was being resolved with loop-closure `start/end` from a previous clip during timeline-follow transitions, which can shift cues early by up to ~1s in gap boundaries.

**Fix applied**
In `apps/desktop/src/components/DesignWorkspace.astro`:
1. `maybeTriggerSplashCue()` now always derives cue bounds from the **current detection** (`reviewStartFor(current)` / `reviewEndFor(current)`) at trigger time.
2. Removed reliance on stale closure window args for cue anchor/pause checks.

**Validation after fix**
1. Re-ran the anchor diagnostics and confirmed data-side anchor drift is zero.
2. Rebuilt desktop app successfully (`npm --prefix apps/desktop run build`).

This is the precise synchronization fix for the “~1s early splash cue” behavior.

1. from __future__ import annotations
2. 
3. import argparse
4. import json
5. from collections import Counter, defaultdict
6. from pathlib import Path
7. 
8. 
9. DEFAULT_OUTPUT_JSON = Path("outputs/event_reviewed_dataset_summary.json")
10. DEFAULT_OUTPUT_MD = Path("outputs/event_reviewed_dataset_summary.md")
11. 
12. 
13. def load_rows(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
14.     return [json.loads(line) for line in path.read_text().splitlines() if line.strip()]
15. 
16. 
17. def summarize(manifest_paths: list[Path]) -> dict:
18.     rows: list[dict] = []
19.     for path in manifest_paths:
20.         rows.extend(load_rows(path))
21. 
22.     by_session: dict[str, list[dict]] = defaultdict(list)
23.     for row in rows:
24.         by_session[str(row.get("source_session_id") or "unknown")].append(row)
25. 
26.     final_label_counts = Counter()
27.     by_session_counts = {}
28.     by_provenance = Counter()
29.     unlabeled = 0
30.     uncertain = 0
31.     agree = 0
32.     disagree = 0
33.     for row in rows:
34.         final = row.get("final_human_event_label")
35.         if final:
36.             final_label_counts[str(final)] += 1
37.             by_provenance[str(row.get("final_human_event_label_provenance") or "unknown")] += 1
38.             if str(final) == str(row.get("suggested_event_label")):
39.                 agree += 1
40.             else:
41.                 disagree += 1
42.         else:
43.             unlabeled += 1
44.         if row.get("suggested_event_label") == "uncertain" or row.get("uncertainty_flag"):
45.             uncertain += 1
46. 
47.     for session_id, session_rows in by_session.items():
48.         by_session_counts[session_id] = {
49.             "row_count": len(session_rows),
50.             "final_label_counts": dict(Counter(str(r.get("final_human_event_label")) for r in session_rows if r.get("final_human_event_label"))),
51.             "reviewed_count": sum(1 for r in session_rows if r.get("human_reviewed_at_event_level")),
52.             "missing_count": sum(1 for r in session_rows if not r.get("final_human_event_label")),
53.             "agreement_count": sum(1 for r in session_rows if r.get("final_human_event_label") and str(r.get("final_human_event_label")) == str(r.get("suggested_event_label"))),
54.             "disagreement_count": sum(1 for r in session_rows if r.get("final_human_event_label") and str(r.get("final_human_event_label")) != str(r.get("suggested_event_label"))),
55.         }
56. 
57.     return {
58.         "total_rows": len(rows),
59.         "counts_by_final_human_event_label": dict(final_label_counts),
60.         "counts_by_session": by_session_counts,
61.         "counts_by_final_human_event_label_provenance": dict(by_provenance),
62.         "remaining_unlabeled_rows": unlabeled,
63.         "remaining_uncertain_rows": uncertain,
64.         "suggestion_vs_final_agreement": {"agree": agree, "disagree": disagree},
65.         "manifest_paths": [str(path) for path in manifest_paths],
66.     }
67. 
68. 
69. def write_md(path: Path, summary: dict) -> None:
70.     lines = [
71.         "# Event Reviewed Dataset Summary",
72.         "",
73.         f"- total rows: `{summary['total_rows']}`",
74.         f"- unlabeled rows: `{summary['remaining_unlabeled_rows']}`",
75.         f"- uncertain rows: `{summary['remaining_uncertain_rows']}`",
76.         f"- agreement: `{json.dumps(summary['suggestion_vs_final_agreement'], sort_keys=True)}`",
77.         "",
78.         "## Final Labels",
79.         "",
80.         json.dumps(summary["counts_by_final_human_event_label"], sort_keys=True),
81.         "",
82.         "## Provenance",
83.         "",
84.         json.dumps(summary["counts_by_final_human_event_label_provenance"], sort_keys=True),
85.         "",
86.         "## By Session",
87.         "",
88.     ]
89.     for session_id, session_summary in summary["counts_by_session"].items():
90.         lines.append(f"- `{session_id}`: `{json.dumps(session_summary, sort_keys=True)}`")
91.     lines.append("")
92.     lines.append("## Manifests")
93.     for manifest in summary["manifest_paths"]:
94.         lines.append(f"- `{manifest}`")
95.     path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
96. 
97. 
98. def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
99.     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Summarize reviewed event manifests.")
100.     parser.add_argument("manifests", nargs="+", help="Reviewed manifest JSONL paths")
101.     parser.add_argument("--output-json", default=str(DEFAULT_OUTPUT_JSON))
102.     parser.add_argument("--output-md", default=str(DEFAULT_OUTPUT_MD))
103.     args = parser.parse_args(argv)
104.     manifest_paths = [Path(path) for path in args.manifests]
105.     summary = summarize(manifest_paths)
106.     Path(args.output_json).write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
107.     write_md(Path(args.output_md), summary)
108.     print(json.dumps({"output_json": args.output_json, "output_md": args.output_md, "total_rows": summary["total_rows"]}, indent=2))
109.     return 0
110. 
111. 
112. if __name__ == "__main__":
113.     raise SystemExit(main())
114.
```

130. def framing(signal: np.ndarray, frame: int, hop: int) -> np.ndarray:
131.     if len(signal) < frame:
132.         padded = np.zeros(frame, dtype=np.float32)
133.         padded[: len(signal)] = signal
134.         return padded.reshape(1, frame)
135.     n_frames = 1 + (len(signal) - frame) // hop
136.     return np.lib.stride_tricks.as_strided(
137.         signal,
138.         shape=(n_frames, frame),
139.         strides=(signal.strides[0] * hop, signal.strides[0]),
140.         writeable=False,
141.     )
142.

144. def local_peak_indices(values: np.ndarray, threshold: float) -> np.ndarray:
145.     if len(values) < 3:
146.         return np.asarray([], dtype=int)
147.     peaks: list[int] = []
148.     for idx in range(1, len(values) - 1):
149.         if values[idx] >= values[idx - 1] and values[idx] >= values[idx + 1] and values[idx] >= threshold:
150.             peaks.append(idx)
151.     return np.asarray(peaks, dtype=int)
152. 
153. 
154. def octave_band_edges(fmin: float = 200.0, n_bands: int = 6, max_freq: float = 8000.0) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:
155.     edges = [(0.0, min(fmin, max_freq))]
156.     low = min(fmin, max_freq)
157.     for _ in range(n_bands):
158.         high = min(low * 2.0, max_freq)
159.         if high <= low:
160.             break
161.         edges.append((low, high))
162.         low = high
163.         if high >= max_freq:
164.             break
165.     return edges
166. 
167. 
168. def spectral_contrast_features(power_post: np.ndarray, freqs: np.ndarray) -> tuple[float, float]:
169.     eps = 1e-8
170.     bands = octave_band_edges(max_freq=float(freqs[-1]))
171.     if len(power_post) == 0:
172.         return 0.0, 0.0
173.     contrasts: list[np.ndarray] = []
174.     for low, high in bands:
175.         mask = (freqs >= low) & (freqs < high)
176.         if int(np.sum(mask)) < 3:
177.             continue
178.         band = power_post[:, mask]
179.         top = np.quantile(band, 0.98, axis=1)
180.         bottom = np.quantile(band, 0.02, axis=1)
181.         contrast = 10.0 * np.log10(np.maximum(top, eps) / np.maximum(bottom, eps))
182.         contrasts.append(contrast)
183.     if not contrasts:
184.         return 0.0, 0.0
185.     stacked = np.stack(contrasts, axis=1)
186.     return float(np.mean(stacked)), float(np.mean(stacked[:, -1]) - np.mean(stacked[:, 0]))
187. 
188. 
189. def onset_flux_envelope(windowed: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
190.     if len(windowed) < 2:
191.         return np.asarray([0.0], dtype=np.float64)
192.     power = np.abs(np.fft.rfft(windowed, axis=1)) ** 2
193.     diff = np.maximum(power[1:] - power[:-1], 0.0)
194.     return np.sum(diff, axis=1).astype(np.float64)
195. 
196. 
197. def tempogram_peak_ratio(onset_env: np.ndarray, min_lag: int, max_lag: int) -> float:
198.     eps = 1e-8
199.     if len(onset_env) < max_lag + 2:
200.         return 0.0
201.     onset = onset_env - float(np.mean(onset_env))
202.     ac = np.correlate(onset, onset, mode="full")[len(onset) - 1 :]
203.     segment = ac[min_lag : min(max_lag + 1, len(ac))]
204.     if len(segment) == 0:
205.         return 0.0
206.     return float(np.max(segment) / max(float(ac[0]), eps))
207. 
208. 
209. def onset_density(onset_env: np.ndarray, threshold_scale: float = 0.5) -> float:
210.     if len(onset_env) < 3:
211.         return 0.0
212.     threshold = float(np.mean(onset_env) + threshold_scale * np.std(onset_env))
213.     return float(len(local_peak_indices(onset_env, threshold=threshold)))
214. 
215. 
216. def extract_features(signal: np.ndarray, sample_rate: int) -> dict[str, float]:
217.     frame = 512
218.     hop = 128
219.     eps = 1e-8
220.     frames = framing(signal, frame=frame, hop=hop)
221.     if frames.size == 0:
222.         return {name: 0.0 for name in PROBE1_FEATURE_NAMES + R2_FEATURE_NAMES + R4_FEATURE_NAMES}
223. 
224.     window = np.hanning(frame).astype(np.float32)
225.     windowed = frames * window
226.     rms = np.sqrt(np.mean(np.square(windowed), axis=1) + eps)
227.     peak_idx = int(np.argmax(rms))
228.     peak_val = float(rms[peak_idx])
229.     mean_val = float(np.mean(rms))
230.     med_val = float(np.median(rms))
231.     std_val = float(np.std(rms))
232. 
233.     peak_threshold = mean_val + 0.5 * std_val
234.     peak_ids = local_peak_indices(rms, threshold=peak_threshold)
235.     transient_peak_count = float(len(peak_ids))
236.     if len(peak_ids) >= 3:
237.         intervals = np.diff(peak_ids).astype(np.float64)
238.         interval_cv = float(np.std(intervals) / max(np.mean(intervals), eps))
239.     else:
240.         interval_cv = 0.0
241. 
242.     frames_120 = max(1, int(round(0.120 * sample_rate / hop)))
243.     frames_300 = max(frames_120 + 1, int(round(0.300 * sample_rate / hop)))
244.     frames_600 = max(frames_300 + 1, int(round(0.600 * sample_rate / hop)))
245.     early = rms[peak_idx + 1 : peak_idx + 1 + frames_120]
246.     late = rms[peak_idx + 1 + frames_120 : peak_idx + 1 + frames_600]
247.     early_mean = float(np.mean(early)) if len(early) else 0.0
248.     late_mean = float(np.mean(late)) if len(late) else 0.0
249.     post_impact_early_to_late_rms_ratio = early_mean / max(late_mean, eps)
250. 
251.     half_level = 0.5 * peak_val
252.     tail = rms[peak_idx + 1 :]
253.     half_idx = next((idx for idx, value in enumerate(tail, start=1) if value <= half_level), len(tail))
254.     tail_half_life_ms = float(half_idx * hop * 1000.0 / sample_rate)
255. 
256.     power = np.abs(np.fft.rfft(windowed, axis=1)) ** 2
257.     post_frames = power[peak_idx : peak_idx + max(1, int(round(0.400 * sample_rate / hop)))]
258.     if len(post_frames) == 0:
259.         post_frames = power[max(0, peak_idx - 1) : peak_idx + 1]
260.     p = np.maximum(post_frames, eps)

327. def evaluate_holdout(model: Any, x_train: np.ndarray, y_train: np.ndarray, x_holdout: np.ndarray, y_holdout: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, Any]:
328.     model.fit(x_train, y_train)
329.     probs = model.predict_proba(x_holdout)[:, 1]
330.     pred = (probs >= 0.5).astype(np.int64)
331.     cm = confusion_matrix(y_holdout, pred, labels=[1, 0]).tolist()
332.     return {
333.         "auc": float(roc_auc_score(y_holdout, probs)),
334.         "macro_f1": float(f1_score(y_holdout, pred, average="macro")),
335.         "accuracy": float(accuracy_score(y_holdout, pred)),
336.         "platform_recall": float(recall_score(y_holdout, pred, pos_label=1)),
337.         "noise_recall": float(recall_score(y_holdout, pred, pos_label=0)),
338.         "confusion_matrix": cm,
339.         "noise_to_platform_fp": int(cm[1][0]),
340.         "platform_to_noise_fn": int(cm[0][1]),
341.         "holdout_probs": probs.tolist(),
342.         "holdout_pred": pred.tolist(),
343.     }

355. def main() -> None:
356.     rows = [json.loads(line) for line in MANIFEST_PATH.read_text().splitlines() if line.strip()]
357.     by_key = row_key_map(rows)
358.     lists = json.loads(LISTS_PATH.read_text())

363.     r6 = json.loads(R6_PATH.read_text()) if R6_PATH.exists() else None
364. 
365.     platform = lists["platform_noise_track"]
366.     train = [RowRef(item["row_key"], item["event_label"], by_key[item["row_key"]]) for item in platform["train_rows"]]
367.     holdout = [RowRef(item["row_key"], item["event_label"], by_key[item["row_key"]]) for item in platform["holdout_rows"]]
368. 
369.     mixed = lists.get("mixed_session_validation_track", {})
370.     reporting_names = mixed.get("reporting_only_slices", [])
371.     sub_slices = mixed.get("sub_slices", {})
372.     reporting_rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
373.     for name in reporting_names:
374.         reporting_rows.extend(sub_slices.get(name, {}).get("rows", []))
375.     reporting_refs = [RowRef(item["row_key"], item["event_label"], by_key[item["row_key"]]) for item in reporting_rows if item["row_key"] in by_key]
376. 
377.     audio_cache: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
378.     fmap: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {}
379.     for item in train + holdout:
380.         sid = str(item.row["source_session_id"])
381.         if sid not in audio_cache:
382.             source_root = resolve_source_root(str(item.row["source_session_root"]))
383.             audio_cache[sid] = decode_audio_mono(source_root / "web" / "session_source_review.mp4", SAMPLE_RATE)
384.         signal = audio_cache[sid]
385.         start = max(0.0, to_float(item.row.get("event_window_start_seconds")))
386.         end = max(start + 0.05, to_float(item.row.get("event_window_end_seconds")))
387.         s0 = int(round(start * SAMPLE_RATE))
388.         s1 = int(round(end * SAMPLE_RATE))
389.         fmap[item.row_key] = extract_features(signal[s0:s1], sample_rate=SAMPLE_RATE)
390. 
391.     x_train = np.asarray([vector_for(item, fmap) for item in train], dtype=np.float64)
392.     y_train = np.asarray([1 if item.label == "platform_dive" else 0 for item in train], dtype=np.int64)
393.     x_hold = np.asarray([vector_for(item, fmap) for item in holdout], dtype=np.float64)
394.     y_hold = np.asarray([1 if item.label == "platform_dive" else 0 for item in holdout], dtype=np.int64)
395. 
396.     np.savez_compressed(
397.         ES4_DATASET_NPZ,
398.         x_train=x_train,
399.         y_train=y_train,
400.         x_holdout=x_hold,
401.         y_holdout=y_hold,
402.         train_row_keys=np.asarray([item.row_key for item in train]),
403.         holdout_row_keys=np.asarray([item.row_key for item in holdout]),
404.         feature_names=np.asarray(ALL_FEATURE_NAMES),
405.     )
